title: CUDA Out of Memory
description: Troubleshooting and resolving CUDA Out of Memory (OOM) errors in PyTorch. This guide provides a systematic approach to diagnosing, fixing, and preventing GPU memory exhaustion during training and inference.
name: CUDA Out of Memory

quick_identification.check: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate X.X MiB
quick_identification.description: PyTorch throws this error when GPU memory is exhausted

quick_identification.check: Training crashes during forward or backward pass
quick_identification.description: Especially with large models or batch sizes
Memory is fully consumed before the error

symptoms.symptom: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate X.X MiB
symptoms.description: The program halts during the forward or backward pass with a PyTorch traceback stating CUDA OOM, indicating that total active allocations exceeded hardware GPU RAM capacity.
symptoms.error_message: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (requested) on device 0 with 8.00 GiB total capacity. No available memory.

symptoms.description: GPU memory is fully consumed, leaving no headroom for new allocations.

root_causes.explanation: Accumulating activation tensors for backpropagation exceeds the available memory capacity on the configured GPU hardware.
recognition_clues: OOM occurs immediately at the start of training
Reducing batch size resolves the issue
root_causes.typical_environment: Training with large models (LLMs, vision transformers) on consumer GPUs

root_causes.explanation: Storing training output tensors containing gradient tracking history in global variables or lists (e.g. logging history without calling loss.item()) prevents the garbage collector from freeing memory.
root_causes.typical_environment: Training loops with improper tensor handling

root_causes.explanation: Repeated allocation/deallocation creates fragmented free memory that cannot satisfy large contiguous requests.
recognition_clues: Memory appears free but allocation fails
Restarting the process temporarily fixes it
root_causes.typical_environment: Long-running training jobs with dynamic tensor sizes

investigation_checklist.description: Run nvidia-smi to see current memory usage
Print memory summary to see active allocations

investigation_checklist.check: Check for gradient tracking in stored tensors
investigation_checklist.description: Ensure loss.item() is called before storing values
Verify batch size is appropriate for model and GPU
Verify if AMP is enabled and working correctly
Verify if model checkpointing is properly configured

diagnostic_commands.purpose: Check GPU memory usage in real-time
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: GPU-Util and Memory-Usage columns show current consumption
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: If Memory-Usage is near 100%, OOM is imminent

diagnostic_commands.expected_output: Detailed breakdown of active, reserved, and free memory
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Look for large active allocations that aren't being freed
Watch for memory growth patterns during training

diagnostic_tests.test: Run a single forward/backward pass and measure peak memory
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Peak memory should be predictable and stable
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: Unstable or growing peak indicates memory leak
diagnostic_tests.next_action: If memory grows, check for gradient leaks

diagnostic_tests.test: Run training with batch_size=1 and measure memory
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Memory usage should be significantly lower
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: If OOM disappears, batch size is the primary cause
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Reduce batch size or implement gradient accumulation

yes.result: Batch size too large - reduce batch size or use gradient accumulation
Memory leak - check for gradient leaks or reference accumulation
Memory fragmentation - restart process or use memory pool

no.result: Check model architecture or data loading for unexpected allocations

solutions.permanent_fix: Implement gradient accumulation to maintain effective batch size
steps: Halve the batch size value (e.g., from 64 to 32).
Enable gradient accumulation step adjustments to compensate for loss representation constraints.
tradeoffs: Smaller batches may reduce training stability
More iterations required to complete an epoch
solutions.performance_impact: May reduce throughput by 20-40% depending on model
solutions.verification: Rerun training execution loop. Verify that epochs complete without traceback warnings.

solutions.quick_fix: Add torch.utils.checkpoint to model forward pass
solutions.permanent_fix: Configure model-level gradient checkpointing for all applicable layers
steps: Wrap expensive operations in checkpoint function
Verify model outputs match between checkpointed and non-checkpointed versions
solutions.performance_impact: Training will be ~20% slower but memory efficient
solutions.verification: Memory usage should drop significantly while maintaining model accuracy.

verification_checklist.description: Memory usage does not grow unboundedly
Model still learns effectively after changes
GPU is not idle due to CPU bottlenecks

practices: Start with small batch sizes and scale up gradually
Profile memory before scaling to full dataset
Set memory limits in training configuration
Implement early stopping on memory thresholds
Log GPU memory usage per epoch
Track memory growth trends over time
Always call .item() on scalar tensors before storing
Use context managers for temporary large allocations
Delete tensors explicitly when no longer needed

common_misconceptions.reality: It only releases free memory back to the GPU allocator, not tensors still in use

common_misconceptions.misconception: OOM always means the model is too large
common_misconceptions.reality: Often caused by memory leaks or fragmentation, not model size

false_positive_cases.why_it_looks_similar: System runs out of RAM, not GPU memory
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Check nvidia-smi - GPU memory will be low, system memory high

false_positive_cases.why_it_looks_similar: Docker/container has memory limit lower than GPU capacity
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Check container memory limit with docker inspect or kubectl describe

false_positive_cases.why_it_looks_similar: Driver crash can manifest as OOM
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Check dmesg and nvidia-smi - driver will show errors

escalation_paths.when_to_use: Model is too large for single GPU even with optimizations
Single model larger than GPU memory
No GPU memory available, must use CPU
tradeoffs: May still run out of CPU memory
